meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.trans: If you want someone to resent, resent Muranishi.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

examples.text: あと、身元引受人が必要なんだけど、母親でいいな？
examples.trans: Also, we need a guarantor to sign you out — your mother works, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.

examples.text: どうしてうちに？うちはアダルトのメーカーだけど。
examples.trans: Why join our place? You know we're an adult video studio, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Godan intransitive verb; 黙ってろ! is a rough 'Shut up!'.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: 分からないことがあれば何でも聞いてください。
examples.trans: If there's anything you don't understand, ask anything.

examples.text: 彼は料理なら何でも作れる。
examples.trans: He can make anything when it comes to cooking.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Points to something visible farther away from both speaker and listener.

examples.trans: That over there is a school.

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: With で (全部で), means 'in total' or 'altogether'.
話してきます combines 話して ('talk and') with きます ('come back') to mean 'I will go talk to them and return'.

examples.text: 少し社長と話してきます。
examples.trans: I will go talk with the president for a bit.

examples.text: ゆっくり話しましょう。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
